title: introduce-model-compatibility-matrix-and-release-assembler
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Onboarding new model variants repeatedly produces implicit compatibility questions (quantized vs fp16, KV-cache layout, tokenizer changes). Manual verification and handwritten release notes cause regressions and slow rollouts. This PR introduces a machine-readable model compatibility matrix plus an automated release assembler that generates profile delta release notes summarizing metadata changes, performance deltas, and recommended downgrade/fallback mappings. Scope: 1) Add compatibility matrix schema and storage for per-model-version compatibility assertions; 2) Add a CI job that runs forward/backward compatibility checks by spinning a lightweight eval harness against a compatibility subset; 3) Add an 'mrctl release-assemble' tool that consumes changed profiles and the compatibility matrix to create a structured release draft and a changelog fragment; 4) Small schema bump for model metadata (compatibility_tags, compatible_with) and accompanying validators. Implementation highlights: - registry/schema/model-metadata.schema.json: add compatibility_tags and compatible_with fields and document semantics; - .github/workflows/compatibility-check.yml: new CI workflow that triggers on PRs touching registry/profiles or schema and runs a matrix of compatible pair tests; - tools/mrctl/cmd/compat_check.go: CLI for local compatibility validation mirroring CI; - tools/mrctl/cmd/release_assemble.go: produces release draft JSON and a markdown changelog fragment, pulls perf deltas via evaluation harness; - scripts/release/assemble_release.py: utility that aggregates profile deltas, annotates with compatibility status, and opens a GitHub release draft via API if GITHUB_DRY_RUN=false; - registry/compatibility/matrix.csv: canonical example matrix template added; - tests/compatibility/test_matrix_integration.py: integration tests for the CI job and assembler. Backwards compatibility: schema change is additive and optional; existing registries continue to function. Rollout plan: feature-gated via MRCTL_COMPAT_MATRIX=on in CI and an opt-in flag in the console; start as alpha for internal model onboarding. Related links: Linear ENG-1294 (compatibility-check harness), ENG-1312 (release-assembler), changes reference the eval-harness repo for perf diffs. Why different from previous work: prior PRs focused on changelog automation or profile generation; this patch centers the registry around an explicit compatibility surface and ties that surface into automated release output to make rollouts and fallbacks explicit and reproducible.
commits: add compatibility matrix schema and example template
implement mrctl compat-check and release-assemble commands
add CI workflow for compatibility checks
schema: add compatibility_tags and compatible_with to model metadata
tests: add integration tests for matrix validation and release assembly
docs: compatibility guide and example runbook
review_comments: Diego Morales: Please add a note on how compatibility assertions interact with pinned rollout policies. Action: added documentation to docs/registry/compatibility.md and updated the compatibility schema description.

Rina Zhou: The CI matrix job timed out in the first run because we were pulling full model weights. We needed to use the lightweight eval subset. Action: switched CI to use eval-harness subset images and added a size limit flag.

Samir Khan: Suggest adding a clear fallback mapping for quantized -> fp16 inference when a variant is incompatible. Action: implemented automatic fallback suggestions in assemble_release.py output and included them in the release fragment.
release_notes: - Introduced a machine-readable model compatibility matrix (registry/compatibility/matrix.csv) and schema fields to record compatibility assertions; - New CI workflow to validate forward/backward compatibility across model variants and tokenizers; - New mrctl commands: compat-check and release-assemble to validate locally and produce release drafts; - Release assembler outputs changelog fragments that include profile deltas, perf regressions, and recommended fallback mappings; - Tests and docs for internal alpha rollout.
